rules.title: Source of income discrimination ban (including Section 8 vouchers)
rules.requirement: Landlords in California cannot refuse to rent to you because of how you will pay rent, including Section 8 vouchers or other rental help. They also cannot charge you a higher deposit, set different terms, or advertise "No Section 8" because of your source of income.
rules.key_value: Source of income, including Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers, is a protected characteristic
rules.coverage_conditions: Most housing in California, including apartments, single-family homes, condos and subsidized housing; applies to landlords, property managers and tenant screening companies.
rules.exemptions: An owner who lives in the home and rents to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics, but may not publish discriminatory advertisements.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (Cal. Gov. Code § 12955)
rules.quoted_span: No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).
rules.penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunctions, access to the denied housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees. File with CRD within 1 year or in court within 2 years.

rules.title: Limits on use of criminal history in tenant screening
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse everyone who has a criminal record. They cannot look at arrests that did not end in a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records. If a landlord denies you because of a conviction, the conviction must be directly related to your ability to be a good tenant.
rules.key_value: No blanket bans; arrests without conviction, sealed/expunged and juvenile records may not be considered
rules.coverage_conditions: Most housing providers in California, including landlords and tenant screening companies.
rules.exemptions: An owner who lives in the home and rents to one additional person is exempt from most FEHA rules.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (Cal. Gov. Code § 12955) and CRD regulations
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.penalty: FEHA remedies: losses, injunction, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, attorney's fees.

notes: The page names FEHA but gives no section numbers. I used Gov. Code § 12955 as the standard citation; please check it. The criminal-history rule also rests on CRD regulations (2 C.C.R. § 12264 et seq.), which the page doesn't cite. The page gives no effective dates, so I left them null. The owner-occupied exemption (owner renting to one extra person) doesn't apply to ordinary apartments, so I put it only in the exemptions text. I left out the other FEHA content (reasonable accommodations, ESAs, familial status, harassment) because it's outside the six categories. The page mentions evictions, rent control and deposits only to say CRD has no jurisdiction over them, so they produced no rules.
